methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates multiple orthogonal approaches: bulk RNA-seq in a discovery cohort (n=103 post-QC), stRNA-seq (n=15 samples from 13 tumors), an IHC validation cohort (n=20), an independent bulk RNA-seq validation cohort (n=59), and an independent pre-surgical biopsy cohort (n=24), plus external TRACERx/TCGA/Uppsala datasets for ITH and survival. Nested cross-validation (100 outer 70/30 splits with inner 5-fold hyperparameter search across GLM/GBM/XGBoost/DRF via h2o AutoML) properly separates feature selection and model choice from final evaluation, and ComBat-seq/reference ComBat are used to control batch and cohort shift. Statistics include negative binomial GLMs with FDR < 0.01, linear mixed models with sample as random effect for spatial spot data, GSEA with Bonferroni, multivariate Cox adjusting for TNM, surgery type, and adjuvant therapy, and a Bayesian (Beta(1,1) prior) projection of PPV/NPV at varying prevalence with 95% credible intervals. Limitations such as imbalanced biopsy design, micropapillary edge cases, and lack of serum/qPCR translation are transparently acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The central question — pre-operative molecular detection of VI in stage I LUAD — directly informs surgical decisions (lobectomy vs sublobar) and adjuvant therapy selection in the JCOG0802/CALGB140503 era, which the authors explicitly link to practice. Evidence from matched biopsy–resection pairs (r=0.77), biopsy AUROC 0.90 (95% CI 0.75–1.0), and prevalence-adjusted NPV of 91% at 30% prevalence provides a plausible, quantitatively supported path to preoperative risk stratification. Findings are multi-cohort retrospective with external validation (discovery, validation, TRACERx, TCGA, Uppsala), placing this at Oxford 2b (individual retrospective cohort with independent validation), not yet a prospective trial, so it is clinically relevant but not practice-changing on its own.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prediction-model development and external validation study, TRIPOD is the applicable standard; most core items are addressed — clearly defined predictors and outcome (histopathology-defined VI), training/validation cohort descriptions, IRB approvals (BU/BMC H-37859; Lahey IRB-518308; Inova U23-06-5093), model form (binomial logit GLM with ridge), handling of batch effects, performance metrics with 95% CIs and bootstrap, and decision-threshold derivation (Youden). Missing items include a TRIPOD checklist, a formal sample-size justification, full model coefficients inline, and a calibration analysis (only discrimination is reported). Data availability is supported by a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary, Source Data files for each figure, external datasets referenced by accession (GSE81089, TCGA via TCGAbiolinks, TRACERx), and code deposited on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.18395868); raw sequencing repositories are redacted in the normalized text so full compliance cannot be verified from this version.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors state that, to their knowledge, VI-associated gene expression has not been previously studied in lung cancer, and they explicitly separate VI from LI within the usually conflated LVI entity — a documented gap. Combining bulk RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics with deconvolution against the Salcher stage I LUAD atlas, dual IHC validation of POSTN/COL1A1 myofibroblasts, ITH assessment in TRACERx, and pre-surgical biopsy feasibility is a novel and well-integrated combination for this question. It is not first-in-class at the method level (each tool is established) and similar EMT/hypoxia aggressiveness signatures exist, which keeps this short of a paradigm shift but clearly above incremental confirmation.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with a logically ordered narrative moving from signature discovery to spatial dissection, cell-type attribution, predictor derivation, ITH robustness, and biopsy proof-of-concept, with each figure tightly mapped to a claim. Figure legends are detailed and specify sample sizes, statistical tests, multiple-comparison corrections, and box/violin definitions, and technical terms (VI, LMP, NST, STAS, LVI) are defined on first use. Prose is concise and precise, limitations (edge cases, biopsy cohort balance, lack of calibration) are acknowledged within the results and discussion, and the abstract accurately reflects the content.

key_strengths: Multi-cohort design with independent bulk validation, external TRACERx/TCGA/Uppsala survival replication, and an independent pre-surgical biopsy cohort showing AUROC 0.90 (95% CI 0.75-1.0)

Rigorous nested cross-validation pipeline (100 outer splits, inner 5-fold hyperparameter search across multiple model families) with reference ComBat harmonization, avoiding common overfitting pitfalls of gene-expression classifiers
Orthogonal biological validation of the signature via stRNA-seq, CytoSPACE deconvolution against the Salcher atlas, spatially weighted regression, and dual POSTN/COL1A1 IHC in a separate cohort
Direct clinical framing against JCOG0802/CALGB140503 era sublobar-resection decisions, with a Bayesian prevalence-adjusted NPV of 91% at 30% prevalence supporting a concrete triage use case
Transparent handling of limitations (edge-case VI+ tumors, balanced biopsy cohort inflating PPV uncertainty, lack of qPCR translation) and code deposit on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.18395868)
key_concerns: Pre-surgical biopsy cohort is small (n=24) and balanced by design, so the headline AUROC 0.90 and PPV estimates have wide credible intervals that only prospective multi-center data can tighten
No calibration analysis for the predictor (only discrimination via AUROC and bootstrap CIs), and no explicit TRIPOD checklist even though the work is a prediction-model development/validation study
Survival associations in TRACERx and TCGA are modest (HRs ~1.7-2.1 per SD) and not consistently independent of TNM stage IA/IB, tempering claims of stage-independent prognostication
Edge cases with lepidic-predominant or >50% micropapillary VI+ tumors were misclassified, and performance degrades in 0%-solid subsets (AUROC 0.70), indicating histology-dependent reliability
Biopsy cohort single institution (Inova) and uses a different library prep kit than discovery/validation, so generalization across preanalytical workflows is not yet demonstrated
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid translational study with a clear mechanistic and clinical narrative, strong external validation, and an honest proof-of-concept biopsy result; content fits Tier 2 (e.g., Nature Communications-oncology, Clinical Cancer Research, JCO Precision Oncology) but falls short of practice-changing Tier 1 evidence because the biopsy validation is small, retrospective, and single-center, and calibration/TRIPOD-level reporting gaps remain.
